fact: The World Bank's record of the additional financing says the project continues an electronic cash-transfer payment system built through a partnership with a financial institution, alongside the Ké-Non management information system and the Unique Social Registry.

The DPSSF states that Programa Família Vulnerável payments to 5,000 households in the first five cycles of 2025, over STN 35.75 million through October, were made by bank transfer using the payments module of the Ké Non system, with BISTP named as the bank.

The DPSSF page describes Kénon as a unified database centralising data on vulnerable families and beneficiaries of programmes such as Programa Família, and as producing reports for both PEP+ and Programa Família; it names no exchange with the ID, civil registration or other government systems. Dated by its published date, 2025-04-22.

The World Bank project paper states that the open-source social protection MIS Ke-Non, deployed in 2024, is integrated with the Unique Social Registry, which holds socio-demographic data on 8,740 families (about 16 percent of the population), and that the MIS tracks beneficiaries, services and payments.
system: Ke-Non (CORE-MIS/openIMIS) integrated with the Unique Social Registry
